ruling: Where a Hebrew name is said to group a set of books, that grouping is honored: the set may be referred to — whole, or by any piece — under that traditional name. The reference claims no piece is the whole; it says the pieces are what the name gathers. The sealed identities beneath are never merged and never renumbered.
ruled_by: the owner, 2026-08-30, in his words: if there is a Hebrew word said to group this set of books, we honor that
entered: typed by hand, in the open, under the ruling above — a reference record, not a text record; it carries no words of any text

retired.by: the owner, in his words: the book of kings thing is an artifact, basically just do it the right way; if we group by i kings then so be it. If anything that's a toggle
retired.what: the door no longer lists a traditional grouping as a row of its own. The ruling of 2026-08-30 that a Hebrew name said to group a set of books may be honored is not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is spending a row on the front door for it while the pieces are their own works and stand as themselves.
retired.if_it_returns: as a toggle inside the work, the way every other alternative reading is offered, and never as a second entry beside the books it gathers

groups_as_they_stood.note: The chain records Kings in two sealed pieces. Either piece is fairly called Book of Kings, and together they are the whole. The two-part division is a printing convention, not the tradition's own.
